sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:88295
Court No. - 89
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 47399 of 2023

Applicant :- Bhimsen
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Ajeet Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.
2.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing entire proceedings of Committal Order dated 19608 of 2021, under Section 376 of IPC, Police Station Binawar, District Budaun passed by Additional Civil Judge (J.D.)/Court No.7 and also summoning order dated 27.09.2022 having Complaint Case No.19608 of 2021 under Section 376 of IPC, Police Station Binawar, District Budaun.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that opposite party no.2 is daughter in law of applicant.
It is submitted that no medical report is brought on record to support the allegation made in complaint.
Witnesses who are produced by the applicant under Section 202 Cr.P.C. are interested witnesses.
No independent witness is recorded.
It is further submitted that there is no evidence of involvement of applicant in the crime.
No case is made out against the applicant.
It is submitted that order impugned is perversed and suffers from manifesto error of law.

sentences.text: applying his mind summoned the accused for facing the trial.

4. Per contra learned Additional Government Advocate opposed the contentions made by learned counsel for the applicants and submitted that the cognizance order has been passed after considering the evidence available on record, therefore, the present application deserves to be dismissed.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and after going through the available record,
the prayer for quashing of the entire proceedings of committal order dated 27.10.2023, cognizance order dated 27.09.2022 is refused.

6. However, it is provided that in case the applicant applies for bail within a period of 30 days from today, his application for bail shall be considered and disposed of expeditiously in view of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
7.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For a period of 30 days or till the applicant surrenders and applies for bail, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant in the aforesaid case.
8. Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed off, accordingly.
